item.title: PLA Eastern Theater Command releases first Taiwan Recovery Day poster, warning against 'Taiwan independence'
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 14:48:00
Photo: Screenshot from the WeChat account of the PLA Eastern Theater Command The Chinese People's Liberation Army (PLA) Eastern Theater Command released its first poster marking Taiwan Recovery Day on Sunday, a move that an expert said sent a clear message that the PLA would not tolerate or show leniency toward any attempts to separate the island of Taiwan from China and would deliver forceful blows against such actions. China formally designated October 25 as the Commemoration Day of Taiwan's Restoration, following a decision adopted at a session of the Standing Committee of the 14th National People's Congress on October 24, 2025, according to the Xinhua News Agency. On Sunday, Taiwan Recovery Day, the PLA Eastern Theater Command released a themed poster titled "Remember Taiwan's Recovery, Defend National Unity" to mark the occasion. Featuring black-and-white documentary photographs, the poster highlights the historical and geographical ties between the mainland and the island of Taiwan, as well as the shared sense of pride and national memory among people on both sides of the Taiwan Straits. A map of Taiwan forms the visual centerpiece of the poster, alongside prominent banners bearing phrases such as "Taiwan's Recovery" and "venue of the surrender ceremony of Taiwan Province of the China war theater of the Allied powers." The message conveyed by the poster is clear: Taiwan's recovery is a shared source of pride for people on both sides of the Straits and part of the collective national memory of all Chinese people, reminding them to remember the history of Taiwan's recovery and defend national unity. Zhang Junshe, a Chinese military affairs expert, told the Global Times on Sunday that the PLA Eastern Theater Command's first-ever poster marking Taiwan Recovery Day had an unmistakable signaling purpose. Zhang said that Lai Ching-te and the Democratic Progressive Party (DPP) authorities stubbornly cling to their separatist "Taiwan independence" position. They not only distort historical facts by "only using the term 'the end of the war' while refusing to acknowledge Taiwan's recovery," but also collude with external forces to spread the false claim that "Taiwan's status remains undetermined," in an attempt to pursue "Taiwan independence by relying on external forces" and "Taiwan independence through military means." With the Takaichi administration's indulgence and active encouragement, Japan's right-wing forces are openly moving to break free from the constraints of the postwar order and accelerating their transformation toward a "neo-militarism." They are also seeking, both openly and covertly, to interfere in the Taiwan Straits, posing a major threat to the postwar international order and peace in the Asia-Pacific region, Zhang said. The message behind the PLA Eastern Theater Command's decision to release a poster commemorating Taiwan's recovery at this particular moment is self-evident, Zhang said. First, it is about safeguarding the historical facts of Taiwan's recovery. The history of Taiwan's recovery to China was a direct result in the victory of the Chinese People's War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression and the World Anti-Fascist War, and is an indisputable historical fact, with all necessary legal procedures fulfilled. Commemorating Taiwan's recovery means remembering the inseparable bond between Taiwan compatriots and the motherland, Zhang said. Secondly, it's about safeguarding the fruits of victory in the war against Japanese aggression achieved by people on both sides of the Taiwan Straits. Today, the PLA will not tolerate any violation of China's sovereignty and territorial integrity, nor will it allow the fruits of victory represented by Taiwan's recovery to be taken away, Zhang said. Third, it is about upholding the mission of safeguarding national reunification. The PLA is an important force in deterring "Taiwan independence" separatist forces and external interference. The PLA will show no tolerance or leniency and will deliver forceful blows against any forces seeking to overturn irrefutable historical facts, undermine national reunification, or pursue the delusion of separating the island of Taiwan from China, Zhang said.

item.title: US labeling of Confucius Institutes a security threat exposes irony of its claimed openness, risks deepening ignorance of China: expert
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 14:00:00
The Pentagon, headquarters for the United States Department of War, is seen on August 13, 2026 in Arlington, Virginia. Photo: VCG The US Department of Defense's decision to designate Confucius Institutes as a national security threat has drawn a sharp rebuke from an official social media account affiliated with China's armed forces, which questioned how learning Putonghua and Chinese culture could pose a threat to the US when American culture is widely embraced in China. A Chinese expert also warned that Washington's move will ultimately undermine America's own ability to understand China. The US Defense Department has designated Confucius Institutes as a threat to US national security, US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth claimed on Friday, Reuters reported. Hegseth, in a video posted on social media, claimed that Confucius Institutes were operating "under disguise of US universities" and that the Pentagon had added them to its list of institutions that threaten US national security, according to Reuters. In response, China Military Bugle, an official press account of China's armed forces replied on X on Saturday, that "If learning Mandarin, KungFu, Chinese calligraphy and dance at Confucius Institutes poses threats to the US, then how many years and how seriously has China been threatened by the US? As so many Chinese learn and speak English, watch Hollywood and Disney movies, and drink Starbucks?" According to statistics from the US Government Accountability Office (GAO), "the number of Confucius Institutes at US universities and colleges declined since 2019, from about 100 to fewer than five. Schools most commonly cited the potential loss of federal funding and external pressures as contributing to their decision to close their Confucius Institute." Schools also cited pressure from US government officials, members of Congress or state representatives among other factors that contributed to their decision, according to GAO. Hegseth's accusations are particularly absurd, as if simply learning Mandarin or exploring Chinese culture could somehow subject American students to Chinese mind control. Such rhetoric reflects a deep insecurity and anxiety about America's own cultural influence and ideological appeal, Chen Hong, director of the Country and Region Studies Institute, School of Foreign Languages, East China Normal University, told the Global Times. Chen noted that what Washington truly fears is not that Confucius Institutes pose a threat to national security, but that Americans might develop an independent understanding of China through direct cultural exchanges - one that challenges Washington's preferred narrative. In recent years, the US has rolled out a slew of measures to stifle normal academic and scientific exchanges between China and the US. China on Friday called on the US to immediately stop its erroneous practice of taking discriminatory and restrictive measures against Chinese research institutions, saying that China would take necessary steps to safeguard the legitimate rights and interests of Chinese research institutions, according to the Ministry of Commerce. The remarks came in response to a media query about research security mitigation results announced by the US Department of Defense on October 19. The announcement said the universities concerned had fully mitigated identified relationships with foreign entities of concern on the 1286 list, which includes many Chinese research institutions. Such actions essentially coerce US research institutions into "taking sides" and deliberately undermine normal scientific cooperation between China and the US, the spokesperson noted, adding that such actions would only backfire on the US itself, undermining its own scientific and technological progress and innovation. In August, the US Defense Department ordered 30 US universities to review their research, financial and academic ties with foreign entities of concern, including Chinese institutions and organizations linked to former Confucius Institutes, warning that failure to comply could jeopardize their eligibility for future federal research funding. Such moves by the US are aimed at creating a "chilling effect," pressuring American universities, scholars and students to engage in political self-censorship when conducting exchanges with China. They will erode the foundation of trust underpinning people-to-people exchanges between the two countries. Ultimately, the US itself will also suffer, because a US that refuses to understand China will only sink deeper into cognitive isolation and strategic miscalculation, said Chen. This also exposes the US' double standards in cultural exchanges and its cultural hegemonic mindset: When the US spreads its values around the world through films, media and education, it is seen as promoting "freedom"; yet when China introduces its language and culture through normal channels, it is smeared as engaging in "ideological infiltration," the expert noted. For a country that prides itself on being a beacon of openness to fear even its own students' interest in learning Chinese and understanding foreign culture is ironic, Chen noted, and stands as a sharp rebuke to America's so-called "cultural confidence."

item.title: 110 humanoid robots set Guinness world record for synchronized dancing in China, eyeing large-scale deployment
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 10:59:00
Photo: Courtesy of AgiBot China's humanoid robot industry is moving from single-machine demonstration toward large-scale coordinated deployment, as 110 humanoid robots set a Guinness World Records title for the most humanoid robots dancing simultaneously in Jinan, East China's Shandong Province, on October 24. The 110 Expedition A3 humanoid robots, developed by Chinese firm AgiBot, performed synchronized dance routines and formation changes using the company's LinkBots cluster-control platform and ultra-wideband (UWB) positioning technology, which enables centimeter-level accuracy. The challenge tested the system's ability to coordinate large numbers of robots while maintaining precise positioning, the company said. During the display, the 110 Expedition A3 robots seamlessly performed a series of synchronized movements, including repositioning, jumping, flips and formation changes, which showcases advances in humanoid robots' spatial movement capabilities. Following the event, the robots will be deployed in cultural and tourism performances, public services, scientific research and education, among other settings, the company said. The significance of such multi-robot demonstrations extends beyond setting records. As Chinese robotics firms improve motion control, positioning and multi-robot coordination, the key challenge is turning these capabilities into reliable real-world applications. Several companies are now exploring large-scale deployment in industrial and service settings. At the World Robot Conference in Beijing in August, Chinese robotics firms demonstrated humanoid robots sorting parcels, handling components and packing mobile phones on production lines. Robotera said it had deployed more than 100 parcel-sorting robots across 15 warehouses, while DexForce reported deploying robots at a Lens Technology factory to pack mobile devices on an assembly line, according to Reuters. However, many applications remain at the pilot or early commercial stage, with reliability, adaptability and cost-effectiveness remaining major challenges to wider adoption. Addressing these hurdles is part of China's broader effort to accelerate the commercialization and large-scale deployment of humanoid robots and embodied AI, industry analysts said. China launched a real-world training initiative in June aimed at promoting the routine deployment of humanoid robots and embodied AI products in real-world production and everyday settings, accelerating their large-scale adoption. The initiative aims to develop more than 100 high-value application scenarios and build the capacity for large-scale deployment of tens of thousands of robots by the end of 2026. At an October 19 press conference, an official with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology said that China had developed more than 400 humanoid robot models and produced over 40,000 units in the first half of 2026. Annual production is expected to exceed 100,000 units, while more than 300 priority scenarios are being targeted for real-world testing and deployment, according to the State Council Information Office. Ultimately, the industry's next test is not simply how many robots can perform in sync, but whether they can carry out useful tasks reliably, efficiently and at scale. Moving embodied AI into real-world jobs requires more than individual technological breakthroughs — it also depends on the ability to train, test and improve robots at scale. Global Times

item.title: China's national civil service exam registration closes, with over 6,000 applicants competing for a single position: media
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-25 10:07:00
Candidates exit the exam venue after the national civil service examination on November 30, 2025. Photo: CNS Photo Saturday marked the final day to apply for China's 2027 national civil service examination, with competition for the most sought-after positions exceeding 6,000 applicants per post, chinanews.com reported on Sunday. As of 5 pm on Saturday, more than 6,000 applicants had passed the initial review for a first-level police inspector position or below with the Yanbian border management detachment of the Jilin immigration inspection general station. The position had only one vacancy, putting the competition ratio at more than 6,000 to 1, according to the report. Yanbian, located in Northeast China's Jilin Province, is the only autonomous prefecture of China's Korean ethnic group, according to the Xinhua News Agency. In addition, several other positions have attracted thousands of applicants for a single vacancy. For example, a position at the Gongyi survey team under the Henan survey team of the National Bureau of Statistics had 5,534 applicants who passed the review for just one opening, with six applications still pending review. According to thepaper.cn, citing statistics from Huatu Education, as of 4 pm on Saturday, 3.025 million applicants had passed the qualification review, bringing the overall average competition ratio to 85 applicants per position. In addition, 83 positions had received no applications by the time registration closed. These "zero-application" positions are concentrated in several types of government agencies, particularly maritime safety administrations, railway police bureaus, and immigration inspection stations under border management authorities, according to thepaper.cn. Some positions at meteorological bureaus, National Bureau of Statistics survey teams, and customs authorities have also received no applications. Such positions typically have strict professional or academic requirements and involve demanding working conditions, such as working on the water, serving in grassroots roles in remote areas, or working shifts. Positions in remote and less accessible regions may also attract fewer applicants, as the pool of who meet the requirements is relatively small. Global Times

item.title: Teodoro charges at China with a paper shield
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-24 13:52:00
Philippines Secretary of National Defense Gilberto Teodoro Jr. delivers his speech during a plenary session of the International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) Shangri-la Dialogue Defense Summit in Singapore, 31 May 2026. Photo: VCG Philippine Defense Secretary Gilberto Teodoro Jr. has once again been huffing at China, claiming that if China were to remove the Philippine ship that is illegally "grounded" at China's Ren'ai Jiao, it would constitute a so-called "act of war." He also warned that if Chinese personnel boarded the vessel, it could trigger the US-Philippines Mutual Defense Treaty. Yet no sooner had he made these threats than he began backpedaling, clarifying that an “act of war” does not necessarily mean the two countries would enter a “state of war,” as “only the President and Congress can declare war.” Teodoro is charging at China with a shield made of paper, only to retreat behind Marcos and the US before China has even made a move. This performance essentially lays bare his opportunism and cowardice. Teodoro's remarks were based on an unverified Philippine media report claiming that “China was considering 10 countermeasures against the Philippines,” including removing the grounded ship, blocking supplies, sanctioning Philippine politicians, reducing oil and fertilizer supplies, and restricting tourism. Teodoro admitted that he had not even read the report, yet he was already rushing to issue warnings. This suggests that he knows perfectly well the price of provoking China and that the Philippines cannot afford to pay it. For all his tough talk, he is effectively crying out in pain in anticipation of the consequences. China has indisputable sovereignty over Ren'ai Jiao and its adjacent waters. The China Coast Guard carries out law enforcement operations to safeguard rights in waters under its jurisdiction in accordance with the law. Its demand that the Philippines remove the illegally grounded warship is legitimate and well-founded. If the Philippines continues to gamble on provocations, persists in illegal intrusions and the reinforcement of structures at Ren'ai Jiao, or even attempts to forcibly break through China's law-enforcement controls, China will certainly take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its territorial sovereignty and maritime rights and interests. The Philippines should harbor no illusions on this matter. The further it goes in provoking China, the heavier the blows it will suffer. By then, it will be too late to try to salvage the situation by hiding behind others. Last month, Philippine media reported on a letter allegedly signed by Teodoro and addressed to a Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) official. According to the reported contents, Teodoro pledged that if he were to assume presidential power in the future, he would continue strengthening the US-Philippines alliance and pursuing a hard-line policy toward China. He also reportedly planned to manufacture maritime friction at Ren'ai Jiao during an ASEAN foreign ministers' meeting to portray China as a country "bullying a smaller nation." The Philippine Department of National Defense promptly denied the letter's authenticity, saying it “is false and fake,” but provided no evidence. The authenticity of the letter remains to be verified. Nevertheless, the pattern of behavior described in it closely mirrors Teodoro's own conduct, lending further weight to the suspicion that Teodoro is "on a mission." He is attempting to manufacture friction to serve his personal political ambitions, using his hardline stance toward China as a token of allegiance to external forces. Before trying to intimidate China with cries of an "act of war," Teodoro had better think carefully about the consequences of his words. No external power will foot the bill for his reckless rhetoric, and any so-called "treaty" will become nothing more than a scrap of paper in the face of risks of this magnitude.

item.title: China issues guidelines to boost AI-driven job creation, mitigate employment displacement risks
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23 19:10:00
Staff members conduct data collection for various scenarios at a company’s embodied?AI robot data collection and training center in Suqian, East China’s Jiangsu Province on September 3, 2026. Through real-robot simulation, on-site operations, and human-robot collaboration, the center precisely captures multi-dimensional core data such as vision, motion, and environment data, laying a solid data foundation for the optimization and iteration of embodied-AI models. Photo: VCG China has rolled out a set of policy measures to create more jobs through artificial intelligence (AI), improve employment quality and mitigate the impact of job displacement resulting from AI applications, helping build an employment-friendly development model, amid the rapid development and growing use of the technology. The guidelines, issued by the General Office of the State Council and made public on Friday, outline 18 major tasks across six areas, covering AI-driven job creation, employment-friendly AI adoption, workforce training, employment services, labor rights and social security protections, and employment risk monitoring and response. The document aims to strengthen AI's positive role in creating job opportunities, enhancing traditional jobs through AI, improving employment quality and stimulating entrepreneurship, while mitigating the impact of AI-related job displacement, according to the guidelines. It also seeks to promote inclusive development by ensuring that technological progress and industrial upgrading go hand in hand with employment growth and improvements in people's livelihoods. To strengthen AI's job creation potential, the guidelines call for expanding employment opportunities in emerging sectors, helping micro, small and medium-sized enterprises retain and expand their workforce, developing new AI-related employment and entrepreneurship models, and accelerating the development of new AI-related occupations. The document also calls for building an employment-friendly pathway for AI adoption, including tapping the employment potential of AI in traditional industries, easing job displacement pressures arising from AI applications and establishing mechanisms to assess employment risks associated with the technology. To improve workers' digital literacy and employability, the guidelines call for coordinated efforts to develop innovative AI talent and the implementation of dedicated AI training programs. In terms of employment services, the document calls for using AI to facilitate the implementation of employment policies, improve the intelligence and efficiency of employment services, and strengthen support for workers transitioning to new jobs or occupations. The guidelines also emphasize improving labor rights and social security systems to keep pace with technological changes. Measures include improving labor rights protections to accommodate human-AI collaboration, improving social security arrangements for flexible workers and those in new forms of employment, and refining income distribution mechanisms to adapt to AI development. To address potential employment risks arising from AI applications, the document proposes strengthening employment risk monitoring and early-warning systems related to AI applications, stepping up research into AI's impact on employment, and improving mechanisms to respond to emerging employment risks. The guidelines call on local governments and relevant departments to implement the measures in accordance with local conditions. Human resources and social security authorities and development and reform departments at all levels are also urged to strengthen coordination to ensure the measures are effectively implemented. The latest guidelines are in line with a five-year plan for implementing the employment-first strategy released by the State Council in June, which called for advancing the "AI Plus" initiative, fostering more entrepreneurial projects involving innovative AI applications and the commercialization of technological achievements, exploring new forms of work involving human-AI collaboration, and strengthening AI's role in job creation. Global Times

item.title: 16 killed, 54 injured after 7.0-magnitude quake hits China's Xizang
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23 10:54:00
CHINA / SOCIETY 16 killed, 54 injured after 7.0-magnitude quake hits China's Xizang By Xinhua Published: Oct 23, 2026 10:54 AM
Sixteen people were killed and 54 others injured after a 7.0-magnitude earthquake struck Baqen County of Nagqu City in southwest China's Xizang Autonomous Region at 10:33 p.m. Thursday. The regional disaster prevention, reduction and relief committee activated a Level III emergency response for natural disaster relief on Friday. The State Council earthquake relief headquarters and the Ministry of Emergency Management also upgraded the national earthquake emergency response from Level IV to Level III. As of 7 a.m. Friday, 11 of the injured were in serious condition, while 43 sustained minor injuries. More than 330 houses collapsed or were damaged. The damage caused by the quake is being further evaluated, and disaster relief work is underway. More than 12,000 residents have been evacuated, according to the city's earthquake relief headquarters. Quake relief supplies allocated by the authorities at various levels have been arriving at the quake-hit zone as of early Friday morning, including 1,000 sets of prefabricated houses, more than 3,200 tents, over 2,800 folding beds, and other daily necessities like quilts, stoves and clothes. The area surrounding the epicenter has an average altitude of more than 4,800 meters. The temperatures there will be as low as minus nine degrees Celsius in the next three days, with intermittent snow expected Saturday in the three townships near the epicenter, according to local weather forecast authorities.

item.title: Ninety years on, the great Long March spirit is a light shining on the world: Global Times editorial
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-23 00:36:00
Marching toward prosperity. Illustration: Liu Rui/GT The great Long March spirit has been deeply etched into the DNA of Chinese society. It is the determination to rise to challenges and to persist for the long haul; it is the courage to fear no sacrifice and to dare to try; it is the clarity to face reality and actively seek change; and above all, it is the original aspiration of standing with the people through life and death, sharing weal and woe, and striving arduously. The 90th anniversary of the victory of the Long March of the Chinese Workers' and Peasants' Red Army was commemorated at a grand gathering in Beijing on Thursday morning. General Secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee Xi Jinping, also Chinese president and chairman of the Central Military Commission, attended the gathering and delivered an important speech. Xi stressed that the great spirit of the Long March demonstrates the power of loyalty, truth, justice and unity. As an important part of the spiritual lineage of the CPC, it transcends time and space and remains evergreen. It will always be a precious treasure and a powerful driving force inspiring us to overcome difficulties and forge ahead courageously. The Long March was a beam of light that burst forth from the Chinese nation at its darkest hour. It showed the world clearly that, even in an old China mired in darkness with no visible way out, there was a group of people striving with all their might to build a new China. In the book The Life Millennium: The 100 Most Important Events and People of the Past 1000 Years, published by the American Time-Life Books, scholars from around the world jointly selected 100 events that shaped the world from 1000 to 2000 AD. The Long March of the Red Army was one of three historical events from China to make the list. It profoundly inspires people that as long as one remains firm in will and unyielding in the face of setbacks, a way out can always be found through continuous exploration, and an entirely new path can be opened. From Edgar Snow to Henry Kissinger, from Nelson Mandela to Fidel Castro, many observers and strategists have pondered why this Long March in the East was able to succeed. To this day, whenever China astonishes the world with technological breakthroughs or reshapes perceptions with development miracles, the world still asks: "How do the Chinese do it?" These questions all point to the same answer: We have found the right path - a path of never yielding, always moving forward, and never retreating. The Long March is both a spiritual treasure that inspires the Chinese people and a display of the Chinese nation's resilient character to the world. Today, the term "Long March" has become a shared name for any arduous journey that ultimately reaches its destination. In this sense, the value of the Long March lies not only in the arrival itself, but in the act of continuing to set forth, again and again. After the victory of the Long March, the nation did not stop: It kept marching through the flames of the War of Resistance Against Japanese Aggression, kept advancing on the tide of reform and opening-up, and continues to advance under the call of the new era, all the way toward the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation. Today, the great Long March spirit has been deeply etched into the DNA of Chinese society. It is the determination to rise to challenges and to persist for the long haul; it is the courage to fear no sacrifice and to dare to try; it is the clarity to face reality and actively seek change; and above all, it is the original aspiration of standing with the people through life and death, sharing weal and woe, and striving arduously. Ninety years on, the great Long March spirit no longer belongs only to history; it is a light that grows ever brighter and shines upon the world. Currently, global governance is experiencing a "darkest hour": climate change, the North-South divide, geopolitical conflicts, and the undercurrents of deglobalization. Old paradigms are failing, and new rules have yet to take shape. Solving many major issues requires long-term planning and sustained effort that transcend political cycles and short-term gains and losses. The spirit of firm conviction, unity and cooperation, and unyielding struggle transcends national borders and ideologies. It inspires humanity to overcome adversity and pursue a brighter future. This both suggests that global governance needs to blaze new trails toward common development, common security, and common prosperity, and helps the world better understand the spiritual bedrock of the Chinese nation, enabling outsiders to better grasp where this "enabling great power" is heading. "Where the spirit lies, there lies the strength." The great Long March spirit resonates with the Chinese nation's cultural tradition of constant self-improvement and has gained new contemporary meaning in the process of Chinese modernization. While it is no longer possible for China today to replicate the march back then, this spirit will always remain, proving to the world that the Chinese nation possesses extraordinary resilience. After decades of struggle, China has long since become the world's second-largest economy and is comprehensively advancing the great rejuvenation of the Chinese nation through Chinese modernization. The enduring national resilience behind the great Long March spirit has been a key factor in creating this development miracle. It is the confidence that allows China to navigate storms and seize the historical initiative, and it also provides a stabilizing expectation for a world full of uncertainty. In the 1980s, Zbigniew Brzezinski, who once served as US national security advisor, walked with his family along the route once taken by the Red Army. He later reflected: "The Long March is more than an epic of almost unmatched heroism." Today, more and more foreigners are coming to China to retrace the Long March route, and places like Loushan Pass have once again become a popular destination for visitors. This is one indication that the great Long March spirit is increasingly needed by the world. As a spiritual monument that the Chinese nation has offered to the world, its importance will become even more prominent in the future. As military writer Wang Shuzeng once described: "The Long March belongs to that category of events in human history which, even after the passage of long years, continue to be sought after by people." "The history of the Long March has never faded; the road of the Long March continues to extend." For China, on the new journey, the Long March has no endpoint. To carry forward the great Long March spirit is to always maintain a high-spirited posture of storming passes and seizing fortresses, to continue the arduous trek on the journey of Chinese modernization, and to respond to all risks and challenges with an unstoppable fighting spirit. It is to both successfully navigate the Long March of our own generation and infuse a world marked by turbulence and transformation with confidence and strength from the East.

item.title: Ukraine's awkward position: Dependent on the US, powerless to push back
item.description:
Published: 2026-10-22 21:22:00
Ukraine Illustration: Liu Rui/GT Tension between the US and Ukraine has once again erupted into the open. Recent remarks by US Vice President JD Vance have laid bare a long-standing yet often obscured reality in US-Ukraine relations: Ukraine is not a formal US ally, and Washington does not want it to join NATO. Vance also called on Ukraine to stop striking Russian energy facilities. His comments appear to mark a clear boundary of US interests underpinning its Ukraine policy. The US may support Ukraine, but that does not mean it will underwrite every demand Kiev makes. Ukraine can rely on American aid, but it cannot expect Washington to stand unconditionally on its side. Vance has not articulated a brand-new policy. His statement is a public restatement of the current US administration's consistent position. The previous US administration, by contrast, stressed the moral imperative of supporting Ukraine, tying Ukrainian security closely to European security and US credibility, fostering a political relationship that resembled an alliance - despite the fact that Ukraine is not a NATO member, nor does it have a mutual defense treaty with the US. That it is not a formal ally has always been true. What stands out now is that the US no longer blurs this line deliberately, but proactively spells it out publicly. "Ukraine is trapped in an awkward, painful position. It cannot do without US assistance, yet it holds no leverage over Washington," Zhang Hong, a research fellow at the Institute of Russian, Eastern European and Central Asian Studies at the Chinese Academy of Social Sciences, told the Global Times. Why is the US choosing this moment to publicly reaffirm this status? The answer lies in Vance's other demand: "Ukraine should stop attacking Russian energy facilities." An earlier diesel fuel deal struck between the US and Russia had already opened rifts in US-Ukraine relations. Compared with Ukraine's battlefield priorities, the US prioritizes its own energy market positioning and domestic political pressures. Compounding this, Washington has delayed deliveries of a batch of weapons to Ukraine. By partially cutting the aid pipeline while explicitly defining the bilateral relationship as non-allied, the US is essentially creating diplomatic cover to ratchet up pressure on Kiev. Should Ukraine's military actions run counter to core US interests, Washington can potentially scale back support and recalibrate its policy, laying full blame for escalation at Kiev's door. Aid is a discretionary favor, while rolling back support is seen as a legitimate policy choice - this has become the underlying logic of the US' Ukraine strategy. This does not mean Ukraine has lost its strategic value to the US. "In the European theater, the Ukraine crisis remains a key instrument for the US to sustain transatlantic security bonds. The US, in turn, retains sway over Europe's security agenda and reaps economic gains from defense industrial cooperation," Zhang explained. Toward Russia, the Ukraine crisis also serves as a vital topic for US diplomatic maneuvering. Whether negotiating ceasefire terms, security consultations or potential future energy and economic accords, Washington keeps the Ukraine crisis alive to preserve room for bargaining with Moscow, he added. Washington's support for Ukraine has never been an open-ended, unconditional moral obligation, but a strategic choice weighed rigorously against costs and benefits. Clearly, Ukraine's interests and grievances are never Washington's priority. Even when it comes to making the kind of deals Washington wants, Ukraine lacks the leverage to deliver. Ukraine's mineral resources available for potential deals are valued at around $500 billion, while potential joint projects between the US and Russia are worth as much as $14 trillion. By comparison, Ukraine's bargaining power is overwhelmingly outmatched. Ukraine has tried to tie itself to Europe, hoping European leaders would lobby Washington to sustain aid. Yet Europe maintains its own interest calculations, and the support it can offer Kiev is steadily dwindling. This leaves Ukraine stuck in a dilemma. The US is deliberately decoupling its own interests from Ukraine's aspirations. It has no objection to continuing to use the Ukraine issue to pressure Russia, yet refuses to assume treaty obligations for Ukraine's security goals. Partnership continues when Kiev's military moves align with Washington's objectives; when interests collide, Ukraine's demands are the ones usually sacrificed. From the moment Washington clarified the boundaries of US-Ukraine relations, one truth emerges: Ukraine has always been a geopolitical tool for the US, never its core interest. This unequal dynamic of dependence and limited bargaining power has left Ukraine in an awkward and passive position from the start.
